question: Can a connected parity start with every junction of size at most seven reach a complete partnered stage of order at least three without outside common candidates?
public_inputs: Full touch census, the sixteen archived explosive starts, and fresh constructions with all initial junctions of size at most seven.
forbidden_inputs: A candidate graph alone cannot certify partnered dynamics. Verify the held blocks and open counts.
A subset can have outside candidates. Check the entire growing end.
primary_observable: First reached stage whose projected law has paired noncandidates, all transversals free, no outside common candidates and correct open counts, or an explicit checked retraction.
cheapest_meaningful_control: The canonical partnered order-three start and a six-point finite binomial stage with some held transversals.
first_executable_signal: Check the literal new six-point stage and its complete next round.
resource_budget: Screen complete first reaches in the touch census and all stored explosive prefixes where full blocks are available; include fresh sampled starts. Stop at a verified history and report bounded screens separately.
decision_or_followup_rule: One lawful reached stage with history, or a sampled bound named by weighting.
stop_rule: One lawful reached stage with history, or a sampled bound named by weighting.
